answer: The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. Each submission hangs on the ridge of a task receipt, and the shale is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. What survives to the tundra is a record of labour, not a list of addresses.
